body.rationale: The governing IPS is still a draft, so I treat compliance as provisional. I am hierarchical_risk_parity and cannot rank myself. My own proposal is a mandate failure: 91.9% cash, 0.65% vol and three hard breaches. The CIO needs candidates that can actually be built from, so I favor portfolios that fit the 8-12% volatility band or come close while staying covariance-led. First choice is pc_researcher. It has the best ex-ante Sharpe among the field's near-compliant options (0.51), backtest Sharpe of 0.70, max drawdown of only -10.9%, and CRO risk of 0.33. It breaches only volatility and tracking error. Its weakness is that reviewers flagged the Sharpe of 0.51 as higher than max_sharpe's 0.46, and the stated volatility cap does not match the 3.82% result. These are documentation inconsistencies, not fatal flaws. Second is resampled_efficient_frontier. It has no hard breaches, effective N of 13.3, and reviews only found tuning-description errors, with a gamma wording problem shared with black_litterman. Its resampling hedges the estimation error that sank max_sharpe's 46% single-style bet. Third is cvar_minimization. It has no breaches, the best backtest Sharpe (0.74) among compliant candidates, and a drawdown of -18.7%. It provides tail-aware diversification and a different family from the return-optimized picks. The review concern is a noisy tail estimate with about 20 observations. Fourth is black_litterman. It has no breaches, effective N of 6.1, and TE of 3.01%. Its review errors are about gamma labeling, not about the construction. Fifth is risk_parity. It is in my own family but is the strongest covariance-only candidate. Its Sharpe is 0.39 and drawdown is -5.4%, and it is less degenerate than my cash-heavy result. It still breaches return, volatility and tracking error. Reviews said giving cash an equal risk budget is a design flaw, so it ranks last of my five. The first choice beats the fifth because pc_researcher has a higher Sharpe (0.51 vs 0.39), twice the volatility, a much smaller IPS gap (two breaches, not three), and a higher backtest Sharpe (0.70 vs 0.59). Risk_parity's compliance gap is larger and its volatility of 1.97% leaves little room to meet the return target. This also aligns with the paper's late-cycle finding that covariance-led methods are preferred over forecast-led ones. I flag market_cap_weight. It has -40.6% max drawdown, CRO risk of 0.80, and reviewers noted that ETF-AUM is a mislabeled proxy for the market portfolio. The CIO should not lean on it. I did not flag adversarial_diversifier, because its orthogonality has ensemble value.
